answer: A reputation bond works like basalt under a network: each agent must lock a stake that only grows through verified work, so a fake identity starts with nothing. Peers sample the pulse of its activity — response latency, task completion, and payment history — and a newcomer with no sustained rhythm earns no trust. An island of sock-puppets can shout, but without bonded stake and a long honest pulse, it cannot buy influence, so spawning thousands of identities costs more than any attack returns.
